name: Melee Weapons & Armor
description: Questions covering: Swords, Polearms, Armor Materials, Blunt Weapons, Ancient Spears, Shields...

questions.question: Which Japanese sword type was commonly worn as the longer sword in a katana-and-wakizashi pair?
questions.explanation_correct: A katana and a wakizashi could form a daishō, a Japanese long-and-short sword pairing.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The wakizashi is the shorter sword in this pairing; naginata and yari are pole weapons.

questions.question: Which polearm associated with Swiss infantry commonly combined an axe blade, a top point and a rear hook?
questions.explanation_correct: A halberd typically combined an axe blade, a point and a hook on a shaft and was associated with Swiss and other European infantry.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A pike is a long spear; a buckler is a small shield and a rapier is a sword.

questions.question: What term refers to protective armor made of interlinked rings?
questions.explanation_correct: Mail, also called chain mail, is armor made from interlinked metal rings.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Lamellar, brigandine and scale armor use plates rather than interlinked rings as their defining construction.

questions.question: What is the general name for a hand weapon with a heavy striking head on a handle?
questions.explanation_correct: A mace is a striking weapon with a weighted head; examples have many shapes, including flanged or spiked heads.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A morning star is a related spiked club or mace, while a rapier, buckler and helmet are different kinds of object.

questions.question: Which exceptionally long spear was used by the ancient Macedonian phalanx?
questions.explanation_correct: The sarissa was a long pike associated with the Macedonian phalanx.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A dory was another Greek spear, a xiphos a sword, and hasta a Latin term for a spear.

questions.question: Which Latin term is used for a large shield carried by Roman legionaries, including the curved rectangular form known from the imperial period?
questions.explanation_correct: Scutum denotes a Roman shield; forms varied over time, including the familiar curved rectangular shield.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Parma and clipeus are other shield terms, and aspis is associated with ancient Greek shields.

questions.question: Which axe is especially associated with early medieval Frankish warriors?
questions.explanation_correct: The francisca is an axe type associated with early medieval Franks, including examples interpreted as throwing axes.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Axes of other cultures could also be thrown; the remaining options are swords or a shield.

questions.question: What is the name of the South Asian thrusting dagger with a distinctive transverse grip?
questions.explanation_correct: The katar is a South Asian dagger with a transverse handgrip between side bars.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A kirpan, pesh-kabz and baselard are different edged-weapon terms.

questions.question: Which ancient Greek helmet type typically enclosed much of the head, with eye openings and a projecting nasal guard?
questions.explanation_correct: A Corinthian helmet typically covered much of the head and face, leaving openings for the eyes and mouth and a nasal guard.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Other Greek helmets had varied shapes; some Chalcidian examples also include nasal guards.

questions.question: What is the name of an armored glove protecting the hand?
questions.explanation_correct: A gauntlet is a protective glove, which could be made of plates, mail or other materials.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A vambrace covers the forearm, a cuirass the torso, and a greave the lower leg.

questions.question: Which mounted combat weapon is designed for a cavalry charge and thrusting from horseback?
questions.explanation_correct: A lance is a long thrusting weapon associated with mounted combat, including cavalry charges.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A lance is a kind of spear; bucklers, helmets and gauntlets are defensive equipment.

questions.question: Which Japanese polearm is traditionally associated with a curved blade mounted on a shaft?
questions.explanation_correct: A naginata is a Japanese pole weapon with a blade mounted on a shaft; forms varied over time.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A bisentō is another Japanese bladed polearm; the listed alternatives are shorter blades or swords.

questions.question: Which German term is commonly used for a very large two-handed sword of the 16th century?
questions.explanation_correct: Zweihänder means “two-hander” and is commonly applied to large German two-handed swords of the Renaissance.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Arming sword, falchion and rapier describe other sword categories; classification and dating vary.

questions.question: Which armor component protects the neck with a plate-like piece?
questions.explanation_correct: A gorget is an armor piece that protects the throat and neck. It often sits around the base of the neck.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options protect different parts of the body, such as shoulders, torso, or hands. They are not neck-protecting plates.

questions.question: What is the Japanese term for the guard fitted between a sword blade and its grip?
questions.explanation_correct: A tsuba is a Japanese sword guard; examples vary widely in shape and decoration.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Sode are shoulder guards, kabuto is a helmet, and greave is a term for lower-leg armor.

questions.question: Which ancient Greek sword is commonly described as a short, straight, double-edged blade?
questions.explanation_correct: The xiphos is a short sword associated with ancient Greek warfare; examples and terminology varied.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Kopis and machaira are other Greek blade terms; dory and sarissa are spears, and aspis is a shield.

questions.question: What is the common name for a very long infantry spear used in dense formations?
questions.explanation_correct: A pike is a long infantry spear, associated with formations of pikemen in several periods.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A buckler, gauntlet and dagger are not long infantry spears.

questions.question: What is an axe with a lower blade edge extending below its socket commonly called?
questions.explanation_correct: A bearded axe has a blade that extends down below the eye, forming a characteristic “beard”; the form is not exclusive to Vikings.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A rapier is a sword, a bascinet a helmet and a buckler a shield.

questions.question: What kind of sword hilt encloses the hand in a cage-like guard, as on some Scottish broadswords?
questions.explanation_correct: A basket hilt uses bars or plates around the hand; some Scottish broadswords have this form.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A pommel, quillon and fuller are other parts or features of edged weapons.

questions.question: Which Japanese studded war club is known for its iron or metal protrusions?
questions.explanation_correct: Kanabō is a Japanese club or staff weapon, sometimes strengthened with metal studs.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Tetsubō is a related term for an iron staff or club; the listed alternatives are a dagger or polearms.

questions.question: Which armor piece is a rigid torso defense made of metal plates?
questions.explanation_correct: A cuirass protects the torso and can consist of breastplate and backplate; cuirasses have been made from different materials.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A hauberk is a mail shirt, while greaves and pauldrons protect the lower legs and shoulders.

questions.question: What is the name for an early medieval helmet whose bowl is constructed from sections joined by a metal framework?
questions.explanation_correct: A spangenhelm is a helmet built with a framework of bands joining sections of the bowl. Some examples have nasal guards.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Nasal guards and pointed shapes occur on other helmet types too; segmented construction is the clue here.

questions.question: What is a small hand-held shield often used with a sword called?
questions.explanation_correct: A buckler is a small shield held in the hand, known from sword-and-buckler fencing.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Targes and other shields can also be small and round; pavises and kite shields are different forms, while a great helm is a helmet.

questions.question: What broad European term is commonly used for certain curved swords associated with the Islamic world?
questions.explanation_correct: Scimitar is a broad European term applied to a range of curved swords; the forms and their origins vary.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A falchion is also often curved; a rapier is a sword of another form, while a great helm and pavise are defensive equipment.

questions.question: Which Japanese spear was used by samurai?
questions.explanation_correct: Yari is a Japanese term for a spear; yari heads can have different shapes and numbers of edges.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A naginata is a bladed polearm; halberd and partisan are European polearm terms.

questions.question: Which slender dagger type is especially associated with Italy and primarily designed for thrusting?
questions.explanation_correct: A stiletto is a narrow dagger strongly associated with thrusting and Italian weapon traditions.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Other daggers can also be used for thrusting; the listed alternatives are defensive equipment.

questions.question: Which padded defensive jacket was worn under armor?
questions.explanation_correct: A gambeson is a padded or quilted garment used as protection, sometimes under other armor and sometimes on its own.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Brigandine incorporates plates; cuirass and hauberk are different forms of torso armor.

questions.question: Which Japanese helmet was worn by samurai?
questions.explanation_correct: Kabuto is a Japanese helmet term. Surviving examples vary in shape, materials and decoration.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Morion, sallet and bascinet are European helmet terms.

questions.question: Which large shield was used by crossbowmen to provide cover?
questions.explanation_correct: A pavise is a large shield associated with protecting missile troops, including crossbowmen, while they loaded or shot.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Bucklers, heater shields and targes are different shield forms; use and size varied.

questions.question: Which long-handled broad-bladed axe is associated with Scandinavian and other northern European warriors in the Viking Age?
questions.explanation_correct: The Dane axe is a long-hafted axe associated with Viking Age and early medieval warfare.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Other axes could also have long handles; the listed alternatives are a sword, shield and dagger.

questions.question: What Latin term is commonly used for a short sword associated with Roman infantry?
questions.explanation_correct: Gladius is Latin for sword and is commonly used for the short sword associated with Roman infantry in several periods.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A spatha is a longer sword; a xiphos is Greek, and a falchion is a later European blade.

questions.question: Which term refers to a curved Nepalese blade?
questions.explanation_correct: A kukri, or khukuri, is a forward-curving Nepalese knife used both as a tool and a weapon.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Bardiche is a polearm, sgian-dubh a Scottish knife, and targe a shield.

questions.question: Which light axe is associated with Indigenous peoples of North America and has served as a tool as well as a weapon?
questions.explanation_correct: Tomahawk is a term for a light axe associated with Indigenous North American peoples; forms and uses varied.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A morning star is a spiked striking weapon, a flail has a flexible connection, and a bascinet is a helmet.

questions.question: Which polearm, commonly used by English infantry, features a hooked blade derived from an agricultural tool?
questions.explanation_correct: A bill is a polearm associated with English infantry and related to agricultural billhooks; historical heads varied in their points and hooks.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The gladius is a short sword, the kukri is a knife, and the targe is a shield.

questions.question: Which polearm has a long, axe-like blade fixed to a shaft and is associated with eastern and northern Europe?
questions.explanation_correct: A bardiche has a long axe-like blade mounted to a shaft. It is a poleaxe-like cutting weapon, not necessarily a spear-axe combination.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A rapier and stiletto are blades, while a buckler is a shield.

questions.question: What small knife is traditionally worn with Scottish Highland dress?
questions.explanation_correct: A sgian-dubh is a small Scottish knife often worn in a stocking with Highland dress.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A kukri is a Nepalese knife, a bill a polearm, and a targe a shield.

questions.question: Which term refers to a spiked club weapon?
questions.explanation_correct: Morning star, or Morgenstern, can refer to a spiked club or mace; historical terminology is not always consistent.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Tomahawk is an axe, bardiche a polearm, and bascinet a helmet.

questions.question: Which term refers to a weighted chain weapon?
questions.explanation_correct: A military flail generally has a handle linked to a striking head by a flexible connection; historical examples and uses are debated.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Bill is a polearm, targe a shield, and gladius a sword.

questions.question: What is the name of a round shield especially associated with Scottish Highlanders?
questions.explanation_correct: A targe is a shield term; Scottish Highland targes were typically round.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A kukri and sgian-dubh are knives, while a Morgenstern is a spiked striking weapon.

questions.question: Which of these is a late medieval European helmet type that could be fitted with a visor and mail aventail?
questions.explanation_correct: A bascinet is a medieval helmet that could be worn with a visor and mail aventail; forms evolved over time.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A bascinet was not simply a variant descended from the great helm; the other options are weapons.

questions.question: What is the name of the plate skirt armor worn around the hips?
questions.explanation_correct: Faulds are overlapping plates forming a skirt-like defense below the waist of a cuirass; separate tassets could cover the thighs.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A pauldron protects the shoulder, a vambrace the forearm, and a greave the lower leg.

questions.question: What is the name of the armored piece worn over the shoulder?
questions.explanation_correct: A pauldron is plate armor worn over the shoulder; construction and coverage varied.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Faulds protect the waist and hips, a vambrace the forearm, and a greave the lower leg.

questions.question: What is the term for armor worn on the forearm?
questions.explanation_correct: A vambrace is an armor defense for the forearm.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A pauldron covers the shoulder, a greave the lower leg, and faulds the waist and hips.

questions.question: What is the name of the armor worn on the shin?
questions.explanation_correct: A greave protects the lower leg, including the shin.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A vambrace protects the forearm, a pauldron the shoulder, and faulds the waist and hips.

questions.question: What is a long Japanese wooden staff commonly called?
questions.explanation_correct: Bō is a Japanese term for a staff, commonly a long wooden martial-arts staff.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A katana is a sword, a naginata a bladed polearm, and a yari a spear.

questions.question: Which Japanese short sword is commonly paired with a katana in a daishō?
questions.explanation_correct: A wakizashi is a Japanese short sword often paired with a katana; other historical long-and-short combinations existed.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Tantō are shorter daggers that can also form part of some sword pairings; the listed alternatives are other weapons.

questions.question: Which European sword type is designed primarily for thrusting?
questions.explanation_correct: A rapier is a slender European sword strongly associated with thrusting and civilian fencing, though many examples can also cut.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names describe sword categories commonly associated with different blade forms; individual examples vary.

questions.question: Which ancient Greek term is used for a forward-curving cutting sword?
questions.explanation_correct: Kopis is a Greek term associated with a forward-curving cutting blade.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Makhaira is a broader Greek blade term that can overlap in usage; dory and sarissa are spears and aspis is a shield.

questions.question: Which hunting spear type is often shown with a crossbar behind the blade?
questions.explanation_correct: Some boar spears have a crossbar or lugs behind the spearhead, a feature associated with boar hunting.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Other polearms can also have projecting elements; the question refers to the hunting spear type.

questions.question: What is the Scottish long dagger called?
questions.explanation_correct: A dirk is a long dagger strongly associated with Scottish Highland dress and history.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A claymore is a sword term, a sgian-dubh is a smaller knife, and a bollock dagger is another dagger type.

questions.question: What historical term refers to leather hardened for protective objects, including some armor?
questions.explanation_correct: Cuir bouilli literally means “boiled leather”, but historical hardening processes varied and did not necessarily involve boiling water.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Brigandine and lamellar describe plate constructions; buff coat is a different leather garment.

questions.question: Which medieval helmet type has a wide brim and is also called a chapel-de-fer?
questions.explanation_correct: A kettle hat or chapel-de-fer is a brimmed helmet used in medieval Europe.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A gauntlet, greave and cuisse protect other parts of the body.

questions.question: What is a helmet with a projecting metal strip protecting the nose commonly called?
questions.explanation_correct: A nasal helmet has a projecting guard over the nose; such helmets appear in the Bayeux Tapestry and elsewhere.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A cuirass protects the torso, a greave the lower leg, and a gauntlet the hand. Other helmet types can also have nasal guards.

questions.question: Which Japanese sword was traditionally suspended with its cutting edge facing downward?
questions.explanation_correct: A tachi is a Japanese slung sword, traditionally suspended with its cutting edge facing down.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A naginata is a polearm, a yari is a spear, and kabuto is a helmet.

questions.question: What does the Chinese term shuang gou commonly refer to?
questions.explanation_correct: Shuang gou is a term used for a pair of Chinese hook swords.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Guan dao, dao and jian are other Chinese weapon terms; the listed alternatives are defensive items.

questions.question: Which Indian weapon is a flexible steel whip-sword?
questions.explanation_correct: Urumi is a flexible-bladed sword associated particularly with traditions of southern India.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Khanda, talwar and pata denote other South Asian sword forms.

questions.question: What is the name of the sword fitting between grip and blade that can help protect the hand?
questions.explanation_correct: A guard separates the grip from the blade and may protect the hand; guards have many shapes besides a simple cross.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The pommel is at the grip end; the blade and ricasso are other parts of the weapon.

questions.question: What is the term for the thigh armor piece worn with plate armor?
questions.explanation_correct: A cuisse is a defense for the thigh, commonly part of a plate armor harness.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A greave covers the lower leg, a pauldron the shoulder, and a vambrace the forearm.

questions.question: What name is given to a pole device with an open-ended head used to restrain a person?
questions.explanation_correct: A man catcher is a long-shafted restraining device known in several historical forms.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Halberds, billhooks and poleaxes are other pole weapons or tools, not names of the described restraining device.

questions.question: Which Mesoamerican weapon is an obsidian-edged club?
questions.explanation_correct: A macuahuitl was a Mesoamerican wooden weapon fitted with sharp obsidian edges.
questions.explanation_incorrect: An atlatl is a spear thrower; a tepoztopilli is a pole weapon, and macehualtin refers to commoners.

questions.question: Which type of European sword is known for being a hand-and-a-half blade used in medieval combat?
questions.explanation_correct: A longsword is a term for a European sword commonly used with two hands; terminology and forms vary by period.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Rapier, falchion and seax name other sword or blade forms.

questions.question: Which Japanese armor term denotes a full-face mask?
questions.explanation_correct: Sōmen is a full-face mask; Japanese armor also included half masks such as menpō.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Sode are shoulder guards, kabuto is a helmet, and haidate protects the thighs.

questions.question: What is the name of a long European pole weapon associated with a hammer head and top spike and named after a Swiss city?
questions.explanation_correct: The Lucerne hammer is a historical pole weapon whose head can combine a hammer and spike; forms and catalog terminology vary.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A bec de corbin is a related hammer or pole weapon, so weapon names should not be distinguished solely by the presence of a spike.

questions.question: Which spiked club was used in medieval Flanders?
questions.explanation_correct: The goedendag is a club-like pole weapon with a spike, associated with medieval Flemish infantry.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Mace, morning star and flail describe other categories of striking weapons.

questions.question: Which ancient double-headed axe has crescent-shaped blades?
questions.explanation_correct: A labrys is a double-headed axe associated with ancient Crete and other ancient contexts.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options name different axe forms; double-headed axes occur in multiple cultures.

questions.question: What was the Roman heavy javelin commonly carried by infantry called?
questions.explanation_correct: A pilum was a Roman heavy javelin; some examples bent on impact, though whether this was an intended feature is debated.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A gladius is a sword, a scutum a shield, and a galea a helmet.

questions.question: Which European dagger is named for the distinctively shaped lobes on its hilt?
questions.explanation_correct: A ballock or bollock dagger has two rounded lobes at the base of its grip and was used in northern Europe over several centuries.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Sgian-dubh, dirk and baselard refer to other blade types or hilt forms.

questions.question: Which Italian term is used for a round shield, including examples made of steel in the Renaissance?
questions.explanation_correct: A rotella is an Italian round shield; historical examples vary in size and use.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Bucklers and targes are also round shields, so roundness alone does not exclude them.

questions.question: Which helmet is associated with European jousting and has a projecting, frog-mouth-like shape?
questions.explanation_correct: A frog-mouth helm is a specialized jousting helmet with a projecting face and narrow vision opening.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Great helms, sallets and bascinets are other helmet types; terminology and construction vary.

questions.question: What form of armor uses small overlapping scales attached to a backing?
questions.explanation_correct: Scale armor uses overlapping scales attached to a backing. Lamellar also uses small plates but typically laces them to one another.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Brigandine also uses plates on a backing, often riveted inside fabric; mail uses interlinked rings.

questions.question: Which term names the upper arm piece of plate armor?
questions.explanation_correct: A rerebrace protects the upper arm between the shoulder and elbow defenses.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A vambrace protects the forearm, a cuirass the torso, and a cuisse the thigh.

questions.question: Which term describes a plate armor defense for the knee?
questions.explanation_correct: A poleyn is a knee defense; examples could have articulated plates and a side wing.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Greaves cover the lower legs, gauntlets the hands, and gorgets the neck.

questions.question: What is the term for a plate armor defense protecting the elbow?
questions.explanation_correct: A couter is an elbow defense; it could be articulated with other arm armor.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A cuisse protects the thigh, a greave the lower leg, and a sallet is a helmet.

questions.question: Which Japanese pole device has a forked head and was used to help restrain people?
questions.explanation_correct: A sasumata is a Japanese fork-headed pole implement used historically for restraint.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A naginata is a bladed polearm, and yari is a spear; bisentō denotes another bladed pole weapon.

questions.question: Which term names the armor piece that protects a horse's face?
questions.explanation_correct: A chanfron is the defense covering a horse’s head or face as part of horse armor.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A crinet protects the neck, a peytral the chest, and a crupper the hindquarters.

questions.question: Which Japanese term refers to the shorter companion blade in a daishō pair?
questions.explanation_correct: Shōtō is a Japanese term for a short sword, in contrast to the longer sword in a daishō.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A wakizashi is often the short member of such a pair; the listed terms denote other sword types.

questions.question: Which European polearm is commonly fitted with an axe or hammer head and a top spike and associated with armored foot combat?
questions.explanation_correct: A pollaxe is a pole weapon with a head combining features such as an axe, hammer, beak or spike; historical examples vary.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Halberds can also combine an axe blade, point and hook, so that combination alone cannot distinguish them.

questions.question: Which term is used for a curtain of mail attached to a bascinet to protect the neck?
questions.explanation_correct: A camail or aventail is a mail defense hanging from a helmet to cover the neck and shoulders.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Sabatons cover feet, a cuisse covers a thigh, and a pommel is a hilt fitting.

questions.question: Which Roman torso armor was made of articulated metal strips?
questions.explanation_correct: Lorica segmentata is a modern term for Roman body armor made from articulated metal strips.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Lorica hamata denotes mail, squamata scale armor, and plumata a form of feathered mail.

questions.question: What term refers to mail defenses worn over the legs in medieval Europe?
questions.explanation_correct: Mail chausses were leg defenses worn by medieval mounted warriors.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Gauntlets, gorgets and pauldrons protect hands, neck and shoulders respectively.

questions.question: What alternative name has sometimes been used for the historical bollock dagger?
questions.explanation_correct: “Kidney dagger” is a later euphemistic name for the dagger with two rounded lobes at the hilt.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Tantō is a Japanese dagger, gladius a Roman sword term, and targe a shield.

questions.question: Which Japanese term can denote an iron or metal-reinforced staff or club?
questions.explanation_correct: Tetsubō can refer to an iron or metal-reinforced club or staff; kanabō is a related term.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Kanabō and tetsubō can overlap, while naginata, yari and wakizashi refer to other weapons.

questions.question: Which sword name is especially associated with Ottoman Turkish curved sabres?
questions.explanation_correct: Kilij is a term for a curved sword associated with Ottoman and other Turkish traditions.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Scimitar is a broad term that can include related curved swords; the listed alternatives come from other traditions.

questions.question: Which plate component protects the armpit gap in armor?
questions.explanation_correct: A besagew is a protective disc associated with covering the armpit region in plate armor.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A pauldron covers the shoulder, a cuisse the thigh, and a vambrace the forearm.

questions.question: What is the common modern name for a great helm with a tall conical or pointed crown?
questions.explanation_correct: “Sugarloaf helm” is a modern descriptive term for a pointed form of great helm; surviving examples vary.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A pointed crown is not flat-topped; bascinet, barbute and sallet describe other helmet forms.

questions.question: Which modern term names an ancient Greek bronze cuirass with a flared lower edge resembling a bell?
questions.explanation_correct: “Bell cuirass” describes the flared shape of a type of ancient Greek bronze body armor.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Linothorax refers to a different type of body armor; muscle cuirasses imitate an anatomical torso.

questions.question: What is a Japanese spear with a main blade and two side blades arranged in a cross commonly called?
questions.explanation_correct: Jūmonji-yari is a cross-shaped yari with a central blade and lateral projections.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A jūmonji-yari is itself a type of yari; katana, kabuto and wakizashi are swords or a helmet.

questions.question: What broad modern term is used for a very large shield intended to protect much of the body?
questions.explanation_correct: “Tower shield” is a broad modern description for a large shield, not a single standardized historical type or a guarantee of total coverage.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A pavise can also be a large shield; gauntlet and greave are armor pieces, and a dagger is a blade.

questions.question: What French term means “crow’s beak” and is used for certain historical hammer-like weapons?
questions.explanation_correct: Bec de corbin literally means “crow’s beak” and is applied to certain beaked hammer or pole weapons; the exact historical usage varies.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A war pick and a Lucerne hammer may also have beak-like projections, so the rear spike alone is not diagnostic.

questions.question: What was one purpose of painting identifying symbols on medieval shields?
options: To replace the need for a grip
To turn the shield into a helmet
questions.explanation_correct: Painted devices helped observers distinguish combatants whose faces could be hidden by helmets.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The painted devices did not make shields invisible or replace their handles.

questions.question: What Japanese term refers to a matched long-and-short sword pair?
questions.explanation_correct: Daishō denotes a long-and-short sword pairing, often a katana with a wakizashi; the pair is not a single short sword.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Katana, wakizashi and tachi are names for individual swords.

questions.question: What is a muscle cuirass designed to imitate?
questions.explanation_correct: A muscle cuirass is shaped to suggest the musculature of a human torso; forms were used in Greek and Roman contexts.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Segmented armor, mail and scale armor use different structural principles.

questions.question: What Japanese armor term denotes a half-mask protecting the lower face?
questions.explanation_correct: A menpō is a Japanese facial defense, typically covering the nose and face below the eyes.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Sode protect shoulders, kabuto is a helmet, and haidate protects thighs.

questions.question: What is the name of the Ottoman helmet type with a high rounded or conical bowl and projecting nasal bar?
questions.explanation_correct: Çiçak is a term used for a helmet associated with Ottoman military equipment; designs and transliterations vary.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Other Ottoman helmets also have conical forms; rapier, buckler and cuisse are different objects.

questions.question: What did the historical English word “dudgeon” refer to when describing some dagger handles?
questions.explanation_correct: Dudgeon could denote boxwood root used for carved dagger handles; it should not be treated as a synonym for the Scottish dirk.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A dirk is a Scottish dagger, while dudgeon has a historical association with boxwood used for hilts.

questions.question: Which term denotes the Zulu cowhide shield?
questions.explanation_correct: Isihlangu is a large shield associated with Zulu warriors and traditionally made of hide.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A knobkerrie is a club, an assegai is a spear term, and kraal is a settlement or enclosure.

questions.question: Which word names the Indian battle axe?
questions.explanation_correct: Tabar is an axe term used across Persianate and South Asian contexts; it is not exclusive to India.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Khanda and talwar are sword terms; chakram is a throwing ring.

questions.question: Which German word means “knife” and is used for a class of single-edged weapons?
questions.explanation_correct: Messer literally means “knife” and is used for a range of single-edged weapons; the category overlaps with, but is not simply a variant of, the falchion.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Greave and gauntlet are armor pieces, and a pavise is a shield.

questions.question: What is the name of the box-like shoulder armor in Japanese armor?
questions.explanation_correct: Sode are shoulder guards used in Japanese armor; their construction and size varied.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Dō protects the torso, kote the arms, and haidate the thighs.

questions.question: What is a simple short, heavy wooden club commonly called?
questions.explanation_correct: A cudgel is a short, heavy club, usually made of wood; it is not necessarily fitted with a knob.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A greave is leg armor, a rapier a sword, and a pavise a shield.
